works.title: Beyond the Rainbow
works.authors: Xuenan Cao and Rafael S. de Souza
works.summary: The Union is scheduled not for next month, not next week, but in one hour. The biometer reads 3.7 lust.
body: The news arrives with both exhilaration and dread: the Union is scheduled not for next month, not next week, but in one hour.
The biometer reads 3.7 lust.
A screen flashes your emotional state: "An unusually high level of anticipation—akin to a lover's lips drawing near for their first kiss."

You have been leaping forward through a harmony few behind you have ever tasted. For most, the biometer stagnates between 1.0 and 1.9 lust—levels commonly achieved while waiting at home for a spouse, aided by the correct dosage of soma. But unlike them, you require little prompting to ascend toward emotional intensity.
There's an old adage: the Union yields 6.0 lust. Yet many doubt whether they truly desire to unify. After all, once achieved, the long-savored suspense dissolves in a blink.
"Your life will change."
Your fellow trainees are ready to celebrate you—this gives a flicker of comfort. But what remains afterward? What will be yours to hold?
"Just imagine what will change after you unify."

Perhaps it is the shedding of an old self. Or the birth of a new one. Who can grasp the spectrum of desires and emotions that come with being spontaneous, vulnerable—truly human? Such fortune is reserved for those who pass every lesson of the Rainbow program, those who possess instinct for ardor.
Photon-rays pierce through a stained-glass window, casting a fragmented rainbow across the floor.

Your recent mood fluctuations—1.0, then 3.6, down to 3.0, spiking to a record 5.1 lust—are smoothed by somatic training. The system annotates this peak with a term previously unknown to you: "Florence syndrome: vertigo experienced when confronted with immense beauty and antiquity, all at once."
Thinking it wise, you take a soma tablet. A gentle, lucid arousal sets in. The biometer levels at 5.0 lust.
The hour arrives. Rain has passed. The air is cool and shimmering with ions. Just minutes remain before you cross into a new world—rising above the unfeeling masses of social primates.
From the Rainbow—a luminous salon where candidates merge with their true selves—comes a voice, sugared and serene:

"Today, we celebrate the brilliance of another alpha. Capable of feeling the full emotional spectrum lost to humankind—A spectrum once sacrificed in pursuit of serenity, A spectrum where rage and grief once stood beside passion and joy. The Rainbow rekindles our capacity for vulnerability, For art, for love. We welcome a new alpha—One who may end the long stagnation That has dulled our species."
The new alpha tries to sit up. Shoulders strain. Hands tremble under the weight of a body not felt in ages. A haze consumes the eyes—then clears.

The world around is barren, lab-like. The alpha leans back against a corroded wall, timeless in its erosion. Surely, the other alphas arrived long ago. But when the alpha glimpses a reflection in the metal—something shudders:
A sagging shell without a biometer.
Skin creased beneath the breasts, around the waist, along the cheekbones and eyes.
Do all alphas look like this?
No one has seen them—only believed in their arrival.
Beyond the Rainbow, there are no maps. Only ambiguity and sorrow.
Searching the room, the alpha stumbles toward what might be a mainframe—or junk metal. The translucent display flickers on:

"Rainbow is a quantum simulation system engineered to map the human limbic matrix via procedural meta-reality generation. As a former subject, you were immersed in a constructed emotional landscape—Escaping the sterile society outside to rediscover the architectures of feeling."
When was I connected?
Something stirs. Before the Rainbow, people turned to artificial pleasures—doses of stimulants to erase fatigue, bitterness, and despair. Depressants. Antidepressants. Mood stabilizers.
A pharmacological equilibrium that made life a flatline.
Rainbow was once a treatment, perhaps—a desperate attempt to reawaken generations dulled to joy and pain alike.
Now, the union of mind and body brings not transcendence but the slow seeping return of despair.
The alpha breathes sharply. Pores sting with the lab's dry heat.
Who keeps this place alive?
Everyone else is still plugged in.
Now, only the alpha remains.
A relic among wires and machines.
Not a savior. A specimen.
The temptation rises: destroy Rainbow.
Burn the lab.
End the illusion, and all the false hope it bears.
But the alpha hesitates. Not now. Not here.
A quiet awareness grows.
Perhaps the work now is to keep Rainbow running—So that one day, another may arrive.
END
footnotes: Lust Units: Logarithmic scale of Strain and Thrill calibrated by the Rainbow system.
Soma: A neural stimulant developed by the entertainment sector to enhance dopaminergic pleasure responses.
